name: Silla
title: Place in Jerusalem associated with the killing of King Joash
summary: Silla is mentioned only once in the Bible, in 2 Kings 12:21, in connection with the murder of King Joash of Judah. Silla was likely a place name or a road in Jerusalem, but in some traditions it has been understood as a person. The biblical text is unclear whether Silla refers to a person or a place, but the name appears in the context of the conspiracy against King Joash.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in connection with the killing of King Joash
keyEvents.description: Silla is mentioned in the account of the murder of King Joash of Judah. Joash's servants conspired against him and struck him down in the house of Millo, on the road leading down to Silla.

keyEvents.title: The conspiracy against King Joash
keyEvents.description: King Joash was killed by his own servants, Josakar son of Shimeath, and Josabad son of Shomer, after he had turned away from the ways of the Lord. Silla is the place or person linked to this event.

keyEvents.title: Parallel account in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: 2 Chronicles gives a parallel account of the conspiracy against Joash, where his servants killed him because of the blood of Zechariah son of the priest Jehoiada.

keyEvents.title: The context of Joash's apostasy
keyEvents.description: After the death of the priest Jehoiada, King Joash turned away from the Lord and began to serve Asherah poles and idols, which eventually led to the conspiracy in which Silla is mentioned.
